newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT -Bunds eye trendline resistance at 102.75.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT -Bunds eye trendline resistance at 102.75.

text.p: June Bund futures traded on LIFFE will remain on Friday within the upward channel that has held the contract since early April, and look towards trendline resistance up to 102.75/76, analysts said.
"There are two trendlines to the upside, the first coming in 102.67 and the second at 102.75," said a futures broker at a German bank in Frankfurt. "The key one is 102.75."
A daily high from February 17 also comes in around this level at 102.76.
At 0659 GMT, June Bund futures were at 102.45, up eight basis points from Thursday's close.
To the downside, the broker said an initial prop for the market came from intra-day suppport around 102.34/35, which coincides with the five-day moving average.
"It looks like the range between 102.34 on the downside and 102.67 to 76 on the upside," he said.
Below 102.34, trendline support comes in at 102.17.
"The long-term trend which started with the lows made on April 4 is a bit far away right now at 101.35," the broker said.
He said the 20-day moving average was also quite far off. That currently comes in at 101.42.
Anil Patel, technical analyst at Nomura International in London, said Bunds were trying to create a higher base and momentum was building up for a move to target 102.79, the high on March 4.

"Daily short-term momentum is overbought so we have to correct that," he said. "We can probably press forward to 103.00, but it all depends on Treasuries, because they backed off (on Thursday) and Bunds are following Treasuries."
He said Bunds had largely ignored estimates that the German tax estimate for 1997 is likely to have a shortfall of 18 billion marks.
At the short end, September Euromark futures were at 96.76, unchanged on the day.
Technical analysts at a European bank in London said there was scope for a push to the low 96.80s.
"Euromarks continue to firm, slowly but surely," they said in a note to clients.
